import { Aside } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

If you need to prove — or debug — that a write on machine A federates to a joined
pot member on machine B, read this first. It collapses a 6-run cross-machine
diagnosis (plan `pot-federation-cross-machine-merge-2026-06-14`, EI-521) into the
traps + the harness.

## Trap 1 — you CANNOT test the merge same-box (the holepunch wall)

Two sidecars on ONE physical host never `peer_connected` — hyperdht holepunch does
not complete between any two endpoints on one box (see
[vm-federation-separate-machine-proof](/internal/docs/agent-insights/vm-federation-separate-machine-proof)).
The same-box pot smokes (`two-instance-pot-from-repo-smoke.sh`) therefore stop
at *join* — they can't exercise the merge. **Do not conclude "the merge is broken"
from a same-box run; it's no-swarm, not no-merge.** Use genuinely separate
machines: `papercusp-desktop/bin/deb-hetzner-federation.sh` (2 Hetzner VMs, public
DHT, destroy-always, ~cents). Creds: `~/.papercusp/hcloud-token`,
`~/.ssh/papercusp-latitude-frame`, `gh` for both identities. Use
`--image=ubuntu-24.04` (EI-503: the bundled pgvector needs glibc 2.38).

## Trap 2 — `peer_connected ✓` does NOT mean federation

The swarm connecting (`[swarm] peer_connected`) is necessary but **not**
sufficient. A write federates only if the full send→receive chain runs:
capture (mig-102 trigger → `substrate_outbox`) → **DRAIN** (`outbox-drain.ts`
appends undrained rows to the own Hypercore log) → swarm replication → peer's
read-merge → projection → PG. If you see `peer_connected` but the row never
appears on the peer, **check `SELECT count(*) FROM harness_shared.substrate_outbox`
on the sender** — a non-zero/undrained count means the drain isn't running (the
bug is the send side, not the swarm).

## Trap 3 — the pot identity PERSISTS across runs (create vs existing)

`pots/from-repo` for a repo whose pot was already published (gist-backed) returns
`existing.kind:'pot'` (a JOIN OFFER with `memberLinks`), NOT `created`. A harness
that only parses `created.hiveSlug` fails on the 2nd+ run. Handle BOTH, and make
**both peers join the SAME pot via A's exact memberLink** (don't have B
re-discover — avoids a stale-pot split). The harness now does this.

## How the harness proves it (once EI-521 is fixed)

`deb-hetzner-federation.sh` (migrated to the pot flow): provision 2 VMs → A
`pots/from-repo` → both `join-link` A's memberLink → `fed_hive_merge_probe`
(write a feature on A, poll B for it origin='remote', **slug-agnostic** because the
pot may remap `harness_slug`) + `fed_plan_part_merge_assert` (flag ON). A WS-DIAG
block dumps the workspace_ids on merge-fail.

## The open bug it surfaced (EI-521)

A joined pot member's captured writes never drain → never federate, even with
`peer_connected` ✓ + same pot topic + both bindings published. Three hypotheses
were tested + REFUTED (saves you re-testing): (a) a spurious sidecar **restart**
(no — fails without it too); (b) **already-booted skips wireOutboxForHarness** (no
— no pre-`boot_federate` step caches the handle, so `bootSingleHarness` runs fresh
and *does* wire the drain); (c) **workspace_id mismatch** (no — outbox + feature +
boot all align at `default`). The live gap: the drain is WIRED but not draining;
the drain query is `drainOutboxOnce` (`outbox-drain.ts:144-151`)
`WHERE workspace_id = handle.workspaceId AND harness_slug = handle.harnessSlug`.
The two open checks (on a live joined member): does the outbox row's `harness_slug`
equal the member's `handle.harnessSlug`, and is `startOutboxDrain`'s LISTEN+poll
loop actually alive? Track in EI-521.

<Aside type="caution">
Each Hetzner run is ~15 min + real cost. Confirm the swarm + capture cheaply
first (the harness logs `[swarm] joined topic` / `peer_connected` + a WS-DIAG),
and prefer one well-instrumented run over run-per-hypothesis. The merge LOGIC +
the per-part cutover are already proven SAME-BOX on real PG
(`plan-part-federation-cutover.integration.test.ts`) — cross-machine only needs to
prove the real-holepunch wire, so scope the run to that.
</Aside>
